title: Boss: PAGE ConsumerLagGrowing billing/orders
summary: Work an on-call page end to end: find the hot partition in the exporter metrics, the poison record in the logs, the recovery plan, and ship the consumer fix that dead-letters instead of blocking.

steps.title: PAGE: ConsumerLagGrowing billing/orders (02:24 UTC)
body: > You are on call. Finance reports that invoices stopped appearing at about 02:10. The billing team is asleep.
$ kubectl logs deploy/billing --since=30m | grep ERR                -> step 2
produce rate on orders: 400 msg/s · one billing pod handles 150 msg/s · 3 pods running · 6 partitions
billing loop today: retry the handler forever on any exception, then commit
1. Name the partition that carries the lag and its share (step 1).
2. Name the poison record(s) from the logs, with how often they failed and why (step 2).
3. Post a recovery plan: can the current fleet drain the backlog, and if not, how many pods (step 3).
4. Ship the consumer fix: bounded retries, then the dead-letter topic with the trace context kept, and never commit
past a record that is neither processed nor parked (step 4).

steps.title: 1. Which partition carries the lag?
prompt: Read the `kafka_exporter` output (Prometheus text format).
Write `string HotPartition(string[] metrics, string group)`:
- use only lines that start with `kafka_consumergroup_lag{` (skip `# HELP`, `# TYPE`, blank lines and other metrics);
- the labels between `{` and `}` are `name="value"` pairs separated by commas; the number after `}` is the lag;
- consider only lines whose `consumergroup` label equals `group`;
- return `"{topic}-{partition} carries {lag} of {total} ({percent}%)"` for the partition with the largest lag (the first
one on a tie), where `percent` is `100 * lag / total` rounded to a whole number;
- if the group has no lag at all (no lines, or a total of 0), return `"no lag for {group}"`.
solution: var rows = new List<(string Topic, string Partition, long Lag)>();
hints: Cut the labels with `IndexOf('{')` and `IndexOf('}')`, split on `,`, then each pair on the first `=` and trim the quotes.
The value after `}` can be parsed with `double.Parse(..., CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)`: exporters may print `48635` or `4.8635e+04`.
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoMetrics = new[]
"# HELP kafka_consumergroup_lag Current Approximate Lag of a ConsumerGroup at Topic/Partition",
"# TYPE kafka_consumergroup_lag gauge",
"kafka_consumergroup_lag{consumergroup=\"billing\",partition=\"0\",topic=\"orders\"} 12",
"kafka_consumergroup_lag{consumergroup=\"billing\",partition=\"1\",topic=\"orders\"} 0",
"kafka_consumergroup_lag{consumergroup=\"billing\",partition=\"2\",topic=\"orders\"} 69",
"kafka_consumergroup_lag{consumergroup=\"billing\",partition=\"3\",topic=\"orders\"} 48635",
"kafka_consumergroup_lag{consumergroup=\"email\",partition=\"3\",topic=\"orders\"} 90000",
"kafka_consumergroup_current_offset{consumergroup=\"billing\",partition=\"3\",topic=\"orders\"} 41877",
"kafka_consumergroup_lag{consumergroup=\"billing\",partition=\"4\",topic=\"orders\"} 900",
Dojo.Eq("the page", "orders-3 carries 48635 of 49616 (98%)", HotPartition(dojoMetrics, "billing"));
Dojo.Eq("another group on the same topic", "orders-3 carries 90000 of 90000 (100%)", HotPartition(dojoMetrics, "email"));
Dojo.Eq("an unknown group", "no lag for fraud-check", HotPartition(dojoMetrics, "fraud-check"));
Dojo.Eq("label order does not matter", "payments-1 carries 30 of 40 (75%)", HotPartition(new[]
"kafka_consumergroup_lag{topic=\"payments\",partition=\"0\",consumergroup=\"ledger\"} 10",
"kafka_consumergroup_lag{partition=\"1\",consumergroup=\"ledger\",topic=\"payments\"} 30",
}, "ledger"));

steps.title: 2. Find the poison record in the logs
prompt: Write `List<string> Poison(string[] logLines, int threshold)`.
- Only lines containing `" ERR "` and `"handler failed"` count. Their `key=value` tokens include `topic`, `partition`,
`offset` and `error`.
- Count failures per record (`topic`, `partition`, `offset`); remember the **last** error seen for it.
- Return the records that failed at least `threshold` times as `"{topic}-{partition}@{offset} failed {n} times ({error})"`,
most failures first (equal counts: topic, then partition, then offset, ascending).
solution: var counts = new Dictionary<(string Topic, int Partition, long Offset), (int Count, string Error)>();
var n = counts.TryGetValue(key, out var c) ? c.Count : 0;
hints: Turn the `key=value` tokens of a line into a dictionary with `Split('=', 2)`.
Key the counts by a tuple `(topic, partition, offset)` and store `(count, lastError)`.

steps.title: 3. The recovery plan
prompt: Post the plan in the incident channel. Write
`string Recovery(long backlog, double producePerSec, double perConsumerPerSec, int consumers, int partitions)`.
- Active consumers = `min(consumers, partitions)`; capacity = active x perConsumer.
- If capacity > produce: minutes = `ceil(backlog / (capacity - produce) / 60)` →
`"drains in {m} min with {active} consumers"`, and if `consumers > partitions` append
`" ({consumers - partitions} idle: more consumers than partitions)"`.
- Otherwise find `needed = floor(produce / perConsumer) + 1`:
- `needed <= partitions` → `"cannot drain with {active} consumers: scale to {needed}, then it drains in {m} min"`
(minutes computed as above with `needed` consumers);
- else → `"cannot drain: even {partitions} consumers handle {partitions x perConsumer}/s < {produce}/s: add partitions or speed up the handler"`
(numbers without decimals).
starter: string Recovery(long backlog, double producePerSec, double perConsumerPerSec, int consumers, int partitions)
solution: string Recovery(long backlog, double producePerSec, double perConsumerPerSec, int consumers, int partitions)
var plan = $"drains in {Minutes(active)} min with {active} consumers";
return consumers > partitions ? plan + $" ({consumers - partitions} idle: more consumers than partitions)" : plan;
return $"cannot drain with {active} consumers: scale to {needed}, then it drains in {Minutes(needed)} min";
return $"cannot drain: even {partitions} consumers handle {partitions * perConsumerPerSec:0}/s < {producePerSec:0}/s: add partitions or speed up the handler";
hints: A local function `Minutes(int n)` avoids writing the drain formula twice.
Format the last message's numbers with `:0`.
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("the fleet already drains", "drains in 16 min with 3 consumers", Recovery(48000, 400, 150, 3, 6));
Dojo.Eq("scale up first", "cannot drain with 3 consumers: scale to 5, then it drains in 8 min", Recovery(48000, 400, 100, 3, 6));
Dojo.Eq("partitions are the ceiling", "cannot drain: even 6 consumers handle 300/s < 400/s: add partitions or speed up the handler", Recovery(48000, 400, 50, 8, 6));
Dojo.Eq("idle consumers are called out", "drains in 1 min with 6 consumers (2 idle: more consumers than partitions)", Recovery(30000, 100, 100, 8, 6));

steps.title: 4. Ship the consumer fix
prompt: Replace "retry forever, then commit" with a loop that cannot block a partition and cannot lose a record.
Write `List<string> Consume(List<(long Offset, string Value, string? Traceparent)> records, Func<string, bool> handler, Func<string, bool> publishDlq, int maxAttempts)`.
For each record, in order:
- call `handler(value)` up to `maxAttempts` times until it returns `true` → `"ok {offset}"`;
- if every attempt failed, call `publishDlq(value)`:
- `true` → `"dlq {offset} after {attempts} attempts traceparent={traceparent}"` (use `-` when there is none: the
dead-letter record keeps the trace context so the failure can be followed);
- `false` → add `"stop at {offset}: dead-letter publish failed"` and **stop** processing (do not commit this record).
- At the end add `"commit {offset}"` with the offset after the last record that was processed or parked, or
`"commit none"` if there was none.
starter: List<string> Consume(List<(long Offset, string Value, string? Traceparent)> records, Func<string, bool> handler, Func<string, bool> publishDlq, int maxAttempts)
solution: List<string> Consume(List<(long Offset, string Value, string? Traceparent)> records, Func<string, bool> handler, Func<string, bool> publishDlq, int maxAttempts)
hints: A `while (!ok && attempts < maxAttempts)` loop counts the attempts.
Only move the commit position after a record is processed or parked; `break` out on a failed dead-letter publish.
Keep the commit as a `long?` so you can tell "none" apart.
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoFlaky = new Dictionary<string, int>();
bool DojoHandler(string v)
if (v.StartsWith("bad")) return false;
if (!v.StartsWith("flaky")) return true;
dojoFlaky[v] = dojoFlaky.GetValueOrDefault(v) + 1;
return dojoFlaky[v] >= 2;
var dojoRecs = new List<(long Offset, string Value, string? Traceparent)>
(41878, "flaky-A3", null),
(41879, "bad-again", null),
Dojo.Eq("the poison record is parked, the partition moves on", new List<string>
"dlq 41877 after 3 attempts traceparent=00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01",
"dlq 41879 after 3 attempts traceparent=-",
"commit 41880",
}, Consume(dojoRecs, DojoHandler, _ => true, 3));
Dojo.Eq("the DLQ is down: stop, commit only what is safe", new List<string>
"stop at 41877: dead-letter publish failed",
"commit 41877",
}, Consume(dojoRecs, DojoHandler, _ => false, 3));
Dojo.Eq("one attempt only", new List<string> { "dlq 1 after 1 attempts traceparent=-", "commit 2" },
Consume(new List<(long Offset, string Value, string? Traceparent)> { (1, "flaky-B", null) }, DojoHandler, _ => true, 1));
Dojo.Eq("nothing to do", new List<string> { "commit none" }, Consume(new List<(long Offset, string Value, string? Traceparent)>(), DojoHandler, _ => true, 3));
Dojo.Eq("blocked at the first record", new List<string> { "stop at 7: dead-letter publish failed", "commit none" },
Consume(new List<(long Offset, string Value, string? Traceparent)> { (7, "bad", null) }, DojoHandler, _ => false, 2));
